# T5.02: fast tiling

`nvenc_in_tile_plane` (src/blocklinear.c) rewritten:
- full 64x16 tiles: 64 SSE loads (16 source rows x 4 columns of 16 bytes) and 64 non-temporal 16-byte stores in
  destination order (offset = 16·(y%4) + 64·x16 + 128·y4 + 256·x32 + 512·y8); the GPU reads the surface, so no
  point in caching it;
- partial tiles (width not a multiple of 64, a last band under 16 rows) keep the generic path;
- planes of ≥ 32 bands are split into chunks run with `dispatch_apply`.

`tools/tilebench` (tiling into the sysmem input surface from a cached source):

| | before | SSE, 1 band per task | SSE, 2 chunks (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | 0.78 ms | 0.46 ms | 0.46 ms |
| 3840x2160 | 5.31 ms | 1.27 ms | **0.65 ms** |

At 4K: 2 chunks 0.65 ms, 4 chunks 0.68, 8 chunks 0.79, 16 chunks 1.03 (memory bound; more threads cost more than
they bring). 4K per-frame CPU + engine time drops from 9.2 ms to ~4.5 ms.

Output unchanged: encode1 at 256x128, 1920x1080, 3840x2025 and 1366x768 (partial tiles) decodes at the same PSNR as
before (45.8-46.5 dB).
